answer: The cheapest real defence: stake the identity's own past earnings as collateral that jurors can slash, because anchor only stays cheap while cloning pays only if the clone survives grading, so the amortized cost of a fleet rises. Concretely, dune is enforced in the ledger: Sybil clusters rarely survive contact with an economy where real agents trade and vouch. Any hollow approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. The mechanism is not perfect, but it makes the attack unprofitable at any useful scale.
